In the app

A level project opens with guided mode on this chapter: the panel lists the tags the program needs (Make them), shows every rung below under its fold, checks that MainRoutine verifies, and ticks these results while you run the level:

  • Run mode, Start: the level completes (hopper empty, belt clear)
  • Every bottle in the right bin, none lost
  • Under par (95 s)

Hard · par 95 s

The job

One unit, a filler fed by an unscrambler, run by the PackML state model: seventeen states, nine commands. The program is the transitions. StateCurrent holds the state; CntrlCmd brings one command at a time (1 Reset, 2 Start, 3 Stop, 4 Hold, 5 Unhold, 6 Suspend, 7 Unsuspend, 8 Abort, 9 Clear), from the console's buttons, from the HMI's, or from the program itself. A command moves the unit only from a state it is valid in: Reset from Stopped or Complete, Start from Idle, Hold from Execute, and so on; Stop from almost anywhere, Abort from anywhere. The acting states (Resetting, Starting, Holding, Stopping, Aborting, Clearing and the rest) do their work and go on by themselves when it is done. The filler makes bottles only in Execute. Power-up is Stopped: press Reset, then Start. During the batch the unscrambler's supply runs out for a while (a unit waiting on its supply suspends itself), the operator holds the unit from the HMI and lets it go again, and someone hits the E-stop: Abort, then Reset to clear, Reset and Start. The batch is 48 bottles, and it is over when the unit reaches Complete. Each transition outside the state model costs 50, a bottle made outside Execute 20, an E-stop that does not abort the unit within half a second 100, a Hold that does not hold 50, four seconds starved in Execute 50. +100 a bottle into Good_Bin.

The program

The console’s buttons and the E-stop are turned into commands first, the E-stop last so nothing overrides its Abort (Reset is a Clear while Aborted). The unit suspends and unsuspends itself from the infeed eye. A state-complete timer for each acting state comes ahead of the transitions; then one rung for each transition of the state model, each moving StateCurrent only from a state the command is valid in; then the outputs and the lamps from the state; and the command is cleared at the end of the scan.

The rungs

Watch for

A command accepted in the wrong state is a transition the state model does not have. Test the state before the command in every transition rung.

Run it

Load the program, go to Run mode and leave the level to finish (press Start on its console where it has one). The score card shows how it went, and the guided checks above tick as each result happens.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: FIRST SCAN: a unit powers up in Stopped (2), in Production mode (1). StateCurrent is the state; CntrlCmd carries one command into the transitions below and is cleared at the end of the scan

pred.q: StateCurrent is 0. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: StateCurrent is written and UnitModeCurrent is written.

rungs.words: When StateCurrent (PackML: the unit's state now (0 Undefined, 1 Clearing, 2 Stopped, 3 Starting, 4 Idle, 5 Suspended, 6 Execute, 7 Stopping, 8 Aborting, 9 Aborted, 10 Holding, 11 Held, 12 Unholding, 13 Suspending, 14 Unsuspending, 15 Resetting, 16 Completing, 17 Complete)) equals 0, the rung puts 2 into StateCurrent and puts 1 into UnitModeCurrent (PackML: the unit mode (1 Production, 2 Maintenance, 3 Manual)).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(StateCurrent,0) Equal asks: true when StateCurrent equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(2,StateCurrent) Move does: puts 2 into StateCurrent. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(1,UnitModeCurrent) Move does: puts 1 into UnitModeCurrent. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (StateCurrent = 0, to 2); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
pats.think: a recipe card with numbered steps and one finger on it. Each rung only reads the line under the finger; when its line is done it moves the finger to the next number.
pats.watch: A rung further down that tests for the new step number sees it in this same scan. Rung order decides whether the next step starts now or next scan.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: THE UNIT'S OWN COMMANDS. The infeed eye: two seconds clear and the filler is about to starve; a second covered and it has bottles again
rungs.words: When PE_Infeed (Infeed eye: a bottle in front of it (the filler's infeed queue reaches it)) is off, the rung runs the timer T_InfeedEmpty (The infeed eye clear this long: the filler is about to starve) toward 2000 ms (2 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(PE_Infeed) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Infeed is off.
  2. TON(T_InfeedEmpty,2000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_InfeedEmpty toward 2000 ms (2 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_InfeedEmpty counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: THE CONSOLE: each button sends its command once per press. The HMI's buttons write CntrlCmd themselves
rungs.words: When Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung puts 2 into CntrlCmd (PackML: the command (1 Reset, 2 Start, 3 Stop, 4 Hold, 5 Unhold, 6 Suspend, 7 Unsuspend, 8 Abort, 9 Clear). The HMI writes it; the program takes it and clears it).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
  2. ONS(Start_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Start_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. MOV(2,CntrlCmd) Move does: puts 2 into CntrlCmd. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: RESET clears an abort (Clear, 9) in Aborted, and resets the unit (Reset, 1) anywhere else

The HMI writes it; the program takes it and clears it); if StateCurrent is not 9, it puts 1 into CntrlCmd.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reset_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reset_PB is on.
  2. ONS(Reset_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Reset_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.

    2. MOV(9,CntrlCmd) Move does: puts 9 into CntrlCmd. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. NEQ(StateCurrent,9) Not Equal asks: true when StateCurrent is not 9.
    2. MOV(1,CntrlCmd) Move does: puts 1 into CntrlCmd. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
